description: Cruiser fills the frame. Tests silhouette, panel density, rim light and material identity. HUD suppressed: this is a look-review frame.
why: BLOCKED ON ONE LINE IN A FILE NO REVIEW STREAM OWNS — D67. THE FIX WAS NEVER LANDED; src/vfx/engines.js:76 still reads `float t = vUv.y;` on 30841d1. Nothing was insufficient and nothing was mis-diagnosed. THE GATE IS `node tools/widediag.mjs close --assert`, which exits 1 while this is true and prints the patch; it agrees with `npm run capture -- --shots close` exit-for-exit (both 1 on close, both 0 on wide, verified). RUN IT ON HARDWARE. Measured on hardware ANGLE/Metal, `node tools/widediag.mjs close --bisect`, 16 single-variable probes over a 57600 px sample, baseline 0.0104/0.0129 at 99.28% near-black: four probes move the frame. Hiding `vfx:ALL` gives 0.1690/0.2621; hiding `vfx:plumes` ALONE gives 0.1689/0.2622, so the plume mesh is the entire source. `post:bloom` off gives 0.1658/0.2600 — bloom is only the vector that spreads it. `msaa:samples=0` gives 0.1688/0.2620 — the mechanism: a partially covered edge fragment has `vUv.y` interpolated at a pixel centre outside the primitive, `pow()` of a negative base is NaN, and `if (edge <= 0.0) discard` cannot catch it because every comparison against NaN is false. The plume instance buffers carry 0 non-finite floats over 2 live instances, so the bad value is NOT in the CPU data. Patching `float t = clamp(vUv.y, 0.0, 1.0);` in at runtime gives 0.1690/0.2621 — the same frame as deleting the plumes outright, which is exactly what a correct clamp should produce. Residue after the sweep: -0.0001. AND THE DEFECT IS RASTER-DEPENDENT, which is why it has survived two waves of review: under NP_RASTER=swiftshader this identical shot renders 0.1692/0.2631 and the clamp is a no-op, while `composerSamples` reads 4 under both. docs/review/look-surface/close.png is a SwiftShader capture (its manifest records fps 4) and is a perfectly good frame — it is not evidence that this one renders. Anyone verifying the fix under SwiftShader will measure no change and wrongly conclude the change is unnecessary. Counterfactual frame: `node tools/widediag.mjs close --with-fix` writes docs/review/widediag-close-clamped.png under a deliberately different name — it is not a frame of this commit and must not be filed as one. THE POSE IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and the plumes are deliberately NOT suppressed in this setup string: suppressing them would turn the shot green and delete the only automated detector this defect has.
setup: const t = N.world.systems.tactical; t.mode='LOCKED'; t.lockTarget = N.world.player; t.yaw = t._yawTarget = 2.35; t.pitchOffset = t._pitchTarget = 0.18; t.zoomT = t._zoomTTarget = 0.02;

description: Mid tactical range, raking key. The everyday playing view. HUD suppressed: this is a look-review frame.
why: Pinned to giant-orbit. The boot default moved from 'giant-orbit' to START_POI ('graveyard') this session, and the graveyard is authored as near-black silhouette and rim — so without this pin every look-review frame silently changed location and stopped being comparable to its committed predecessor.

description: The cruiser as a small bright hull against a ringed gas giant, seen ACROSS the combat plane. The shot that sells the game: scale comes from a recognisable object in front of an enormous one, so the ship has to stay identifiable and the giant has to fill the frame.
why: REFRAMED. This used to be 'maximum tactical zoom' at zoomT 0.86, and 'maximum tactical zoom' and 'the frame that sells the game' are the same control wanting opposite things. The pitch floor rises with zoom (ORBIT.pitchFloorMax 0.95 over smoothstep(0.30, 1.00, zoomT)), so at 0.86 the camera looked 58 degrees DOWN at an empty plane against a 23 degree half-FOV; measured, the giant sat at ndc.y 2.21, 43.2 degrees off axis, entirely out of frame. Three things fix it and none of them touches the tactical camera's feel:  (1) the shot names the POI it needs — the boot default moved to START_POI ('graveyard'), which has no gas giant at all, so the shot's own yaw solve was falling back to a guessed 1.7 rad at a place with nothing to point at;  (2) the stand-off is stated in METRES and solved back through the camera's own zoomRange(), so a retune of the zoom curve moves the shot's zoomT and not its framing;  (3) the view elevation is stated in RADIANS and solved back through pitchFloor(), for the same reason. Measured at 20000 m / 0.20 rad: giant on screen at ndc [0, -0.15], 3.6 degrees off axis, angular radius 39.6 degrees; cruiser 74 px tall in a 900 px frame; luma 0.052, contrast 0.104, near-black 69.1%, clipped 0.00% — clear of all three of capture.mjs's guards.
setup: const t = N.world.systems.tactical; t.mode='LOCKED'; t.lockTarget = N.world.player; const STANDOFF_M = 20000; const ELEVATION_RAD = 0.20; const g = N.world.systems.celestials?.parts?.giant?.object; if (!g) throw new Error('shot `wide` needs a POI with a gas giant; got poi=' + (N.world.systems.travel?.currentPOI ?? '?')); const p = g.position; const h = Math.hypot(p.x, p.z) || 1; t.yaw = t._yawTarget = Math.atan2(-p.x / h, -p.z / h); const zr = t.zoomRange(); t.zoomT = t._zoomTTarget = Math.log(STANDOFF_M / zr.softMin) / Math.log(zr.max / zr.softMin); t.pitchOffset = t._pitchTarget = ELEVATION_RAD - t.pitchFloor();

description: Chase camera. Tests the cinematic framing and the sense of mass.
Cruiser under way with hostiles on the plane. Tests scale cues and the fight read.
why: Deliberately NOT pinned to a POI: this one is about the fight, so it should show wherever the game actually starts.
setup: const w = N.world; const t = w.systems.tactical; t.mode='LOCKED'; t.lockTarget = w.player; t.yaw = t._yawTarget = 0.4; t.pitchOffset = t._pitchTarget = 0.42; t.zoomT = t._zoomTTarget = 0.48; const foe = w.ships.find(s => s !== w.player && !s.dead); if (foe) { w.player.orderAttack(foe); foe.orderAttack(w.player); }

description: Close pose WITH the interface up. The occlusion frame: diff it against `close` to measure what share of the hull the chrome is standing on.
why: Same pose and same POI pin as `close`, so the diff is exactly one CSS property. Blocked by the same defect D67 and unblocked by the same one line in src/vfx/engines.js:76 — see `close`'s note for the 16-probe bisect and the SwiftShader control that prove it, and `node tools/widediag.mjs hud-close --assert` for the gate. Until that lands, the occlusion diff cannot be computed: subtracting a HUD frame from a black frame measures the HUD, not what the HUD is standing on.
